functions.description: Parse the amount of substance in moles from raw question text, handling scale words and units with exact factors.
inputs: raw text giving the amount of substance with unit, e.g. 7.39 mol
outputs: amount of substance n in mol

functions.description: Parse the gas volume from raw text including its unit and convert it exactly to litres.
inputs: raw text giving the volume with unit, e.g. 0.03256 m3

functions.description: Parse the absolute temperature from raw text and convert it exactly to kelvin, applying the Celsius, Fahrenheit and Rankine offsets and scales.
inputs: raw text giving the temperature with unit, e.g. 507.15 K

functions.description: Provide the molar gas constant R expressed in L·atm/(mol·K) for use with volume in litres and pressure in atm.
Compute the ideal gas pressure p = nRT/V from amount, gas constant, temperature and volume using exact decimal arithmetic.
inputs: amount of substance n in mol

functions.description: Cross-check an ideal gas pressure by recomputing nRT/V in SI units and comparing it with the primary pressure.
inputs: amount of substance n in mol

functions.description: Solve the ideal gas law pV = nRT for the pressure of a gas given its amount, volume and absolute temperature.
inputs: the amount of substance n of the gas with unit (moles)
the volume occupied by the gas with unit
the absolute temperature of the gas with unit
outputs: pressure of the gas in atm

entry_points.text: Using pV = nRT, find the pressure of ●1 of C2H6 occupying ●2 at ●3.

params.description: the amount of substance n of the gas with unit (moles)
params.validity_range: Must be a positive finite number of moles (n > 0). Zero or negative amounts are physically meaningless. Parse scale words such as millimol or kmol with exact factors.

params.description: the volume occupied by the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Must be a positive finite volume (V > 0). Units such as m3, dm3, L, mL and cm3 must be converted with exact factors (1 m3 = 1000 L, 1 dm3 = 1 L, 1 L = 1000 mL = 1000 cm3). Unhandled units must raise an error.

params.description: the absolute temperature of the gas with unit
params.validity_range: Must be an absolute temperature above 0 K (T > 0). Kelvin values must be positive. Celsius values must be above -273.15 °C and are converted by adding 273.15. Fahrenheit values must be converted with the appropriate offset and scale. The ideal gas law is only approximate near condensation or at very high pressure.
